stories.title: Constitutional law expert brands defence bill allowing secret security rules ‘lazy and irresponsible’
summary: Anne Twomey says lack of proper debate around bill is ‘flabbergasting’ amid concerns over extension of ministerial powersLabor’s new defence bill is “lazy and irresponsible” lawmaking, one of Australia’s leading constitutional scholars has warned, claiming provisions for the government to secretly class any facility as a special security zone could raise serious legal issues.Prime minister Anthony Albanese claimed on Monday that critics of the ‘accelerating capability and protecting bases’ bill were “jump[ing] at shadows”, accusing them of “absurd” claims.

But parliamentary crossbenchers opposed to the bill, which was rushed through parliament with little public scrutiny, were joined on Monday by Prof Anne Twomey, who expressed alarm about what she called an increasing trend of ministers exercising discretionary powers without parliamentary oversight.

stories.title: Monday briefing: What could Andy Burnham’s reset mean for the UK?
summary: Nobody really wants to think about Brexit any more, save for the original Brexiters, who seem delighted that Andy Burnham’s “reset” with the EU has given them an excuse to get the old gang back together.

But arguments about whether the UK should rejoin the EU will reignite in parliament this week, as Burnham briefs MPs on the deal he agreed on Friday.That deal wasn’t so much a victory as the culmination of Keir Starmer’s incrementalist approach to UK-EU relations.
Its core agreements haven’t been ratified by member states yet, and the EU won’t sign them off until Britain resolves a dispute over tuition fees for European students.

summary: This blog is now closed‘Very difficult to bridge that divide’: Murray WattCabinet minister Murray Watt says it’s increasingly difficult to bridge the divide between nations on climate policy after a frustrating Cop summit that didn’t reach a final agreement.It’s obviously a very deeply disappointing outcome that the cover decision was not agreed to by all nations.I think what this shows is a very challenging international environment at the moment to reach agreement on almost anything and particularly a situation like this where you’ve got fossil fuel producers on the one hand and other countries that are experiencing very serious impacts from climate change.We’re seeing much greater defence engagement between Australia and Japan, Australia and the Philippines, and the Philippines and Japan.Even though I think it doesn’t quite come across in its overall score, that US defence relationship in the region is stronger, which is helping Australia.
